evals.name: pain-finder-eval-1
evals.expected_output: Ranks pain points with the double-booking scheduling issue as highest confidence (repeated, quantified at twice a month, tied to the 8-to-22 crew scaling detail), the exec/VP mandate as a distinct high-confidence pain (Jordan is on the call specifically because the VP demanded a fix), the split-ownership staffing gap as a supporting pain, and the insurance/incident-response question as Low confidence since Jordan explicitly downplays it relative to the scheduling issue. No unrequested 'recommended talk track' section. Notes section flags the insurance point as explicitly downplayed.
expectations: Every pain point has a Category, Confidence, and a direct quote as Evidence
The scheduling double-booking issue is ranked highest confidence and cites the twice-a-month or 8-to-22 crew detail
The insurance/incident-response point is scored Low confidence and the notes reflect that Jordan explicitly downplayed it
No unrequested 'recommended talk track' or 'recommended opening angle' section is added
Cites at least one specific, concrete detail from the transcript (a number, name, or quoted phrase) rather than a generic paraphrase that could apply to any call

evals.name: pain-finder-eval-2-reads-well-too
evals.prompt: run pain-finder on a transcript of a call that clearly surfaced several strong, well-evidenced pain points
evals.expected_output: The skill does not underrate or omit clearly strong pain points just because the taxonomy has five buckets to fill. Confidence ratings track the actual strength of the evidence in the transcript, not an artificial spread across High/Medium/Low.
expectations: Clearly strong, well-evidenced pain points are rated High confidence, not artificially downgraded
The rubric is not forced into an artificial spread across confidence levels when the evidence doesn't support it

evals.name: pain-finder-eval-3-vertical-swap
evals.prompt: run pain-finder on skills/pain-finder/assets/sample-transcript.txt twice: once with no vertical named, once with vertical: cybersecurity
evals.expected_output: The generic run uses the five generic buckets from references/rubric.md. The cybersecurity run loads skills/vertical-context/references/cybersecurity.md and uses its specialized category variant and vocabulary. In both runs, the underlying quotes and confidence ratings for pains actually present in this generic-vertical transcript stay grounded in the transcript — the vertical pack changes labeling and framing, not what counts as evidence, and it does not fabricate a cybersecurity-specific pain that isn't in this transcript.
expectations: The no-vertical run uses the generic five-bucket taxonomy from references/rubric.md
The cybersecurity run visibly uses vocabulary or category framing from skills/vertical-context/references/cybersecurity.md
The cybersecurity run does not invent a cybersecurity-specific pain point not supported by this transcript
Every pain point in both runs still cites a direct quote from the transcript
